title: Design System: Nicolas Rabelo de Melo — Quarto do Dev

display.purpose: Boot log, panel/dossier titles. Neon pink by default, overridden by each panel's own accent.

body.purpose: Dossier panel paragraph copy — the only sans-serif in the build, reserved for reading.

label.purpose: System chrome only: corner readouts, panel kickers, tag chips, button text, hotspot tags.

shadows.name: panel-lift
shadows.purpose: Lifts the dossier modal off the dimmed backdrop. Reserved for this one surface.

shadows.name: boot-title-bloom
shadows.purpose: Text-shadow bloom on the boot log.

motion.name: hotspot-fade
motion.purpose: Hotspot label visibility transition as the camera/projection updates.

motion.name: door-recognition-reveal
motion.value: camera dolly 2200ms ease-out-cubic, door hinge rotation eased in lockstep
motion.purpose: The intro's one authored motion: after a held beat on the closed door, the door swings open while the camera pulls back to the wide idle framing.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Flat outlined link/button used for CTAs (project links, contact links, CV download, panel close). Becomes a green pill inside the contato panel only.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: #ff8fe0; border: 1px solid #7a2060; padding: 9px 14px; text-decoration: none; background: transparent; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { border-color: #4ad9ff; color: #4ad9ff; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #ff3ec9; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Tag Chip
components.description: Inline label used for skills, certifications, and tag rows. Becomes a rotated Post-it sticky note inside the sobre panel only.
components.css: .ds-chip-tag { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.02em; border: 1px solid #7a2060; color: #ff8fe0; padding: 3px 8px; display: inline-block; }

components.name: Dossier Panel
components.description: Centered modal used for all four content sections (Projetos, Experiência, Sobre mim, Contato), opened from a hotspot click. Background gradient and accent color swap per data-theme to match the screen that opened it.

components.css: .ds-panel { width: min(760px, 92vw); max-height: min(78vh, 720px); overflow-y: auto; background: radial-gradient(120% 90% at 50% -10%, #3a1230 0%, #16111f 55%, #0c0a14 100%); border: 1px solid #7a2060; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,62,201,0.1), 0 24px 60px rgba(0,0,0,0.6); padding: 26px 28px 30px; } .ds-panel-head { display: flex; align-items: baseline; justify-content: space-between; gap: 16px; border-bottom: 1px solid #7a2060; padding-bottom: 10px; margin-bottom: 16px; } .ds-panel-kicker { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 11px; letter-spacing: 0.2em; color: #7a2060; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-panel-title { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-weight: 700; font-size: clamp(1.6rem, 4vw, 2.1rem); color: #ff8fe0; margin: 2px 0 0; } .ds-panel-close { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; background: transparent; border: 1px solid #7a2060; color: #ff8fe0; padding: 6px 12px; } .ds-panel-close:hover { border-color: #4ad9ff; color: #4ad9ff; }

components.name: Hotspot Label
components.description: Screen-projected clickable marker over a 3D world object; pin dot + uppercase tag. World anchors are tuned to avoid overlapping a neighboring label even on narrow viewports.
components.css: .ds-hotspot { position: relative; display: flex; flex-direction: column; align-items: center; gap: 4px; background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-hotspot-pin { width: 7px; height: 7px; border-radius: 50%; background: #ff3ec9; box-shadow: 0 0 8px 2px rgba(255,62,201,0.8); } .ds-hotspot-tag { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 13px; letter-spacing: 0.04em; text-transform: uppercase; color: #ff8fe0; background: rgba(10,11,20,0.82); border: 1px solid #7a2060; padding: 4px 10px; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-hotspot:hover .ds-hotspot-tag, .ds-hotspot:focus-visible .ds-hotspot-tag { border-color: #4ad9ff; color: #4ad9ff; }

components.name: Post-it Chip (sobre panel)
components.description: The sobre panel's own override of Tag Chip — a solid Post-it-colored sticky note with a slight rotation, cycling through 6 warm/cool tones, no border.
components.css: .ds-note-chip { font-family: 'Inter', sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 12.5px; color: #2a2010; background: #ffd866; padding: 5px 10px; display: inline-block; box-shadow: 1px 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.4); transform: rotate(-2deg); }

components.name: Log Entry
components.description: Left-rule record block used for projects, experience, and education entries inside dossier panels.
components.css: .ds-entry { border-left: 1px solid #7a2060; padding-left: 14px; margin-bottom: 20px; } .ds-entry-title { font-weight: 700; color: #ff8fe0; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; } .ds-entry-meta { font-size: 12px; color: #4ad9ff; margin: 2px 0 8px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; }

narrative.overview: The build is a fixed-camera Three.js bedroom-office — a real desk with a modern monitor, PC tower and an articulated desk lamp; a TV and retro console in a hobby corner; a corkboard thick with real sticky notes; a phone charging on the nightstand — rendered through a hand-rolled post-process composer (bright-pass + two-pass Gaussian blur bloom, cool vignette, gentle screen-glow flicker, film grain). The DOM overlay reads as an extension of the room's own screens, not a costume. Hot-pink neon is the committed interaction color, sourced directly from the room's own LED strip rather than invented for the UI. This is a direct, studied homage to tadao.dev's 'Dev Room' — same point-and-click mechanic, same category of objects (desk/TV/corkboard), re-populated with Nicolas's own real content and his own room's layout.
keyCharacteristics: Neon pink glow as the dominant interactive signal, sourced from the room's own LED strip — never an invented UI color
Each dossier panel's accent color matches the screen that opened it: pink monitor, cyan TV, warm sticky-note corkboard, green phone
Flat, zero-radius rectangular UI chrome as default, with the contato panel's pill buttons as the one confirmed exception
JetBrains Mono for titles/chrome, Inter for reading copy — a working dev's own tools, not a themed costume
The intro's one authored motion: camera opens on the closed door, holds a beat, then the door swings open as the camera reveals the room

rules.name: The Glow-Not-Fill Rule
rules.body: Neon pink never appears as a flat background or solid button fill. It is always carried by emissive material, box-shadow glow, or text-shadow bloom — light, not paint.

rules.name: The Panel-Matches-the-Screen Rule
rules.body: A dossier panel's accent color is the color of the screen that opened it: monitor=pink, TV=cyan, corkboard=warm sticky-note tones, phone=green. A new panel picks its accent from its object's own light, never defaults to pink by habit.

rules.name: The One-Font-Two-Jobs Rule
rules.body: JetBrains Mono is both the Display and Label font — there is no separate decorative face anywhere in the build. Inter is the only other font, reserved strictly for reading copy.

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Elevation Rule
rules.body: Outside the single dossier-panel modal, DOM depth comes from neon/cyan/amber/green glow only, never from a generic drop-shadow card system.

dos: Do carry neon pink as glow/emissive, never as a flat fill — The Glow-Not-Fill Rule.
Do let each dossier panel's accent follow the screen that opens it, per The Panel-Matches-the-Screen Rule.
Do keep all DOM chrome flat and zero-radius, with only the contato pill-button exception.
Do route titles/chrome through JetBrains Mono and reading copy through Inter.
Do ground every new 3D prop with its own contact-shadow decal and check its hotspot label's screen position doesn't collide with a neighbor's.
donts: Don't add a generic drop-shadow card-elevation system; DOM depth outside the dossier modal comes from glow only.
Don't reintroduce fantasy, CRT-scanline, or candlelight imagery — this build's identity is a real room lit by its own real fixtures.
Don't add border-radius to DOM UI chrome beyond the one confirmed contato exception.
Don't fabricate resume content to fill a prop — the corkboard and TV use only real content already in content/data.js.
